column1: # THE CAP TABLE -- who owns the shares of WOOL-VENTURE-1. Append-only.
# *** SCOPED TO ONE VENTURE, NOT TWO -- THE PLAYER'S OWN SPLIT, DAY 103. ***
# "The shares you're talking about are just for the initial wool purchase at
# the floor and selling in Ludbury, then giving a share of the profits to the
# 6 holders and Wend. Those accounts are all settled, closed." That is
# wool-venture-1: the day 12-16 buy and the day 25-27 Ludbury sale.
# EVERYTHING SINCE -- the standing floor-price wool buy under art.7 and the
# cloth-making plant -- is `ongoing-venture` in campaign/venture.tsv, and it
# has NO ROW HERE. Checked against the record, day 103: nobody but the party
# has put capital into it, and Wend's pay for running it is a WAGE, not a
# share (rolls.tsv, day ~33: she was offered the choice, "buy a share or take
# a wage, her choice" -- wool_venture.md settles which: "Wend runs it on a
# wage and has said plainly she has never worked a loom"). A wage is not a
# claim on profit, so ongoing-venture has no cap table to keep.
# *** "SETTLED, CLOSED" HAS ONE OPEN TAIL. *** campaign/venture.tsv still
# carries `venture_payable_holders`, 229 gp, flagged rather than assumed
# discharged -- loop L003 opened day 34 naming this exact sum and has no
# close row as of day 103. This file's own table below is not in doubt; the
# question is only whether the LAST STEP of paying it out ever got logged.
# *** WHAT A SHARE MEANS HERE, PRECISELY. *** wool_venture.md, "The shares":
# capital returns off the top BEFORE anything is divided (CAPITAL RETURNS
# FIRST), and only the PROFIT that remains after that is split by share. A
# share is a claim on profit, not on capital or physical stock.
# *** WHO PUT IN CAPITAL, AND WHO DID NOT. *** THE PARTY put in the 450 gp
# that bought the clip (day 12-16) -- all of wool-venture-1's capital is the
# party's own coin. WEND put in no coin: she took a full share "backing her
# own judgement" rather than the 20 gp fee offered (d6=1). Her share is
# EARNED, not bought. THE HOLDERS put in no coin either: they chose "the
# floor price and a share" over "a good price and no share" for their WOOL,
# which the party bought from them AT THE FLOOR -- the wool itself was a
# sale to the party, not an investment in it. Their share is the PRICE of
# that choice.
# So: 14 shares, one class, no capital weighting -- because no share was ever
# priced against capital put in. Pricing what a share is "worth" is
# valuation, and the player was explicit: figure that out when needed, not
# routinely.
# *** THE SIX HOLDERS ARE ONE ROW, `holders_six`. *** wool_venture.md names
# four of six by description -- "Rell's brother, Ellery, Marrow, Ferd's old
# master, and two more" -- and Rell's brother and Marrow resolve to people.tsv
# (gyll, marrow). The other two are NEVER NAMED IN THE RECORD. Splitting six
# shares across four knowns and two unknowns would invent an allocation nobody
# agreed to, which this project does not do. `holders_six` is a documented
# bucket, not a person, and it is closed vocabulary the same way `party` is in
# carry.tsv.
# who     a character name (characters.tsv), a people.tsv id, `holders_six`,
#         or `wend`.
# verb    anchor (sets outright) | move (adds, negative to remove -- a share
#         sold or transferred)
# shares  in units of a WHOLE share; Hask and Dellie hold half each per the
#         day-16 agreement (henchmen draw half where PCs draw full, the same
#         line characters.tsv already draws for experience and treasure)
